Severe Flooding Disrupts Cable & Satellite Facilities in Odisha

Heavy monsoon rains have triggered severe flooding across parts of Odisha this week, causing significant disruption to the Cable & Satellite industry's operations in the region. Several ground stations, uplink centres and regional broadcasting hubs have been directly affected, forcing firms to halt or scale back core activities.

At least four major facilities operated by leading industry players such as SkyBeam Digital, HorizonSat India, and Eastern Cable Services remain inundated, with waters breaching key equipment rooms and damaging on-site transmission infrastructure. Company representatives confirmed that both permanent and contractual staff have been unable to safely access the sites, with emergency teams working around the clock to secure assets and limit further losses.

"Our main uplink facility in Cuttack has been under water since early Tuesday morning," said Shankar Rao, Operations Head at HorizonSat India. "We have evacuated all non-essential personnel and are monitoring the situation closely. The safety of our workers and the integrity of our broadcast equipment are our top priorities."

According to the Odisha Cable & Satellite Workers Union, more than 200 industry employees are directly impacted, with many awaiting further instructions as floodwaters continue to rise. "This is an unprecedented event for our members," said union spokesperson Priya Mishra. "We are coordinating with management to ensure all necessary precautions are taken."

Industry analysts estimate that up to 60% of local cable and satellite transmission capacity is currently disrupted. With rainfall expected to continue over the next 48 hours, the full extent of the damage remains uncertain.

Companies have begun contingency planning, but restoration efforts will depend on weather conditions in the days ahead.
